chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Husayni narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far Ahmad ibn Isa ibn Abi Maryam al-Ajali informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Ziyad al-Azrami narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Hatem al-Manqari narrated to me, from Hisham ibn Salim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: "And We place the Scales of Justice for the Day of Resurrection, and so no soul shall be treated unjustly at all."
He said: They are the Prophets and the Successors, peace be upon them.

key_terms.فَلَا تُظْلَمُ نَفْسٌ شَيْئًا: And no soul shall be treated unjustly at all

ai.seo_question: Who are the 'Scales of Justice' mentioned in the Quranic verse about the Day of Resurrection?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) offers a distinctive ontological interpretation of the 'Scales of Justice' (Al-Mawazeen al-Qisṭ) mentioned in Surah Al-Anbiya, identifying them not merely as physical instruments but as the Prophets and their Successors (Al-Awsiya). This view underscores the Shia doctrine that divine justice is mediated through the infallible Imams, who ensure that no soul is wronged in the final reckoning. The hadith highlights the pivotal role of the Ahl al-Bayt as the living embodiment of God's equitable judgment on the Day of Resurrection.
